gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies the same forcing-data defect: general L2 data lack representative-independent endpoint values and time derivatives, while the estimator theorem requires spline data. It also recognizes that the algorithm and optimality claims are therefore undefined or unsupported and proposes a compatible restriction or redesign with data oscillation.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries identify the mismatch between the advertised general L2 forcing class and the endpoint/derivative evaluations and spline regularity required by the time-stepping scheme and estimator theory.

component_coverage.gold_component: The scheme and estimator are not defined or justified for the stated general L2 forcing class because endpoint representatives and time derivatives are unavailable, while the proof requires spline data.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states the endpoint and derivative failure for L2 equivalence classes, the stronger spline assumption used only by the estimator theorem, the resulting failure of the algorithm and optimality guarantee, and a repair addressing both restricted data and general-data treatment.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 identifies that the eigenmode proof assumes a positive real H-orthogonal spectral basis and, in infinite dimensions, a complete discrete eigenfamily not supplied by ellipticity alone. It gives the same failure of the inf-sup proof and the same self-adjointness and compactness repairs.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries identify the unsupported eigenbasis/eigenvalue-by-eigenvalue inf-sup argument under merely elliptic operator assumptions, including the missing self-adjoint spectral structure and infinite-dimensional discrete completeness.

component_coverage.gold_component: The inf-sup proof relies on a positive real H-orthonormal eigenbasis and a complete discrete spectrum that are not implied by the stated ellipticity assumptions, especially in infinite dimensions.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly distinguishes ellipticity from the required real positive orthogonal eigenbasis and infinite-dimensional compact/discrete spectral hypotheses, ties that gap to the eigenvalue-by-eigenvalue proof, and supplies the corresponding repair or an alternative operator proof.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns a false right-endpoint norm equivalence for invisible temporal polynomial modes and the resulting failure of the full-space, mesh- and eigenvalue-uniform inf-sup bound, with an initial-trace correction. ISSUE-005 instead concerns V_h-star stability of a reduced-space projection in a quadrature estimate; it does not diagnose endpoint-value norm equivalence, invisible modes, or the initial-trace obligation.

ISSUE-004 identifies that full-space differences are not elements of the reduced trajectory space, so the theorem's reduced-space norms and cross-space triangle inequality are ill-typed, and it also recognizes the missing comparison needed for an ambient norm repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries identify the undefined reduced-space norm applied to V_h-valued errors and projections, together with the fact that replacing it by an ambient norm requires an additional norm comparison not supplied by the reduced inf-sup argument.

component_coverage.gold_component: The reduced-basis error theorem applies X_R norms to differences that are generally not reduced-valued, making the assertion ill-formed; an ambient or restriction-based norm and comparison are required.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that the errors are not V_R-valued, that the stated norms are undefined, that the ambient X_h norm is not automatically controlled because of the restricted dual norm, and that an explicit ambient/restriction-based repair is needed.
